title: Experience is presented to embodied self-models

statements.text: The Hard problem may require an account of selves. Brains infer mental spaces and populate them with body-centric representations of sensation and action, so experiences are presented to inner experiencers in the form of embodied self-models with degrees of agency, which partly vindicates quasi-Cartesian intuitions.

sources.quote: it may also be the case that addressing the Hard problem requires understanding the nature of selves
these experiencers may take the form of a variety of embodied self-models with degrees of agency
